info.name: VoApps DirectDrop Voicemail API
info.description:
# VoApps DirectDrop Voicemail API

Ready-to-run requests for the VoApps REST API, built from the **API Access Guide** in the [VoApps Knowledge Base](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html). Every request description quotes the guide's parameter tables and links back to its guide page, so the Knowledge Base stays the source of truth: [https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html).

- **Base URL:** `{{base_url}}` = https://directdropvoicemail.voapps.com/api/v1

- **Authentication:** `Authorization: Token token=<your_api_key>`, the format the API Access Guide documents, set once on this collection (Authorization tab) from the `api_key` variable. The previous version of this collection sent a Bearer token from a variable named `API key`; if you imported that one, import this version again and set `api_key`.

- **Collection revision:** 2026-10-06. Guide content quoted as of that date; if a request here ever disagrees with the guide, the guide wins.

## Set up in 3 steps

1. **Get your API key.** Log in to your DirectDrop Voicemail account, select the **API Access** icon and click **Show Key** ([Accessing Your API Key](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/accessing-your-api-key)).

2. **Paste it into `api_key`:** open this collection's **Variables** tab (or the optional **VoApps API** environment) and paste the key as the **Current value**. Partners also set `partner_api_key`.

3. **Run the Smoke Tests.** Open **Smoke Tests (run in order)** and run the folder, or click Send on **01. GET | List Accounts**. It confirms your key works and fills in `account_id` for the steps that follow.

## How the collection is organized

| Folder | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Smoke Tests (run in order)** | 31 numbered steps in five parts: read-only checks, a test campaign and record, optional campaign controls, partner checks, and error handling. |
| **Accounts, Messages, Caller Numbers, Campaigns, Transactional Records, Partner API** | One folder per guide section, with every variant (filters, date formats, pagination, result codes). |
| **Not in the guide** | Requests from the old collection that the guide does not document. |

The numbered **Smoke Tests** are the ordered run. The other folders hold individual reference requests (every filter, date format and variant), best sent one at a time.

Request names use the same method labels as the Knowledge Base sidebar: `GET`, `POST`, `FORM POST`, `JSON POST`, `PUT`.

## Safe by default

- Campaigns are created with `confirm=false`: the guide describes this as testing campaign creation **without delivery**. Set `confirm_campaign` to `true` only when you want a campaign to run.

- `verified_by_user` (the Caller Number Certification) defaults to `false`; the collection never makes that certification for you.

- Cancel requests and account creation are blocked until `confirm_cancel` / `confirm_create_account` is `true` (the guide documents no way to undo a cancel or remove an account).

- A request is skipped (not sent), with a plain-English message in the **Postman Console**, if a variable it needs is empty (for example, `account_id` before List Accounts). The same happens to blocked Cancel and Create an Account requests.

- The sample phone number (`111-555-1010`) and postback URL (`your-url.example.com`) come from the guide and are not real.

## Variables

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `base_url` | VoApps API base URL. Every request starts with {{base_url}}. |
| `api_key` | REQUIRED. Your API key (DirectDrop Voicemail account > API Access icon > Show Key). Sent as: Authorization: Token token=<your_api_key>. |
| `partner_api_key` | VoApps partners only. A separate credential from your account API key. Used only by the Partner API folder. |
| `account_id` | The account to work in. Filled in automatically by "GET \| List Accounts" (or type it). |
| `message_id` | A message in that account. Filled in by "GET \| List Messages" or "FORM POST \| Create a Message". |
| `caller_number_id` | A caller number's internal id (used only to address the caller-number endpoints). Filled in by "GET \| List Caller Numbers". |
| `voapps_caller_number` | The caller number as a phone number, e.g. +15555551212. Campaigns and records take this, not the caller number id. Filled in by "GET \| List Caller Numbers". |
| `campaign_id` | A campaign in that account. Filled in when you create a campaign or list campaigns. |
| `record_id` | A record in that campaign. Filled in by "JSON POST \| Create a Record". |
| `partner_user_id` | Partners only: the managed user to act on behalf of (sent as the VOAPPS_API_USER_ID header). Filled in by "GET \| List of Partner Users". |
| `account_timezone` | Timezone for "POST \| Create an Account". Must be one of the supported timezone strings. |
| `new_caller_number` | The phone number you want to register with "POST \| Create a Caller Number", e.g. 555-555-1212. |
| `phone_number` | Phone number used by the record requests (the guide's sample number). Replace it to test real delivery. |
| `voapps_zip_code` | Recommended on records: zip code that helps VoApps respect the contact window. |
| `voapps_voice_append` | Alphanumeric value spoken at the end of the message (the guide's sample). |
| `voapps_postback_url` | Webhook URL that receives each record's result (the guide's sample; replace with your own HTTPS endpoint). |
| `campaign_pace` | Pace (successful deliveries per hour, 50 to 8000) sent when creating a campaign. |
| `campaign_new_pace` | Pace sent by "PUT \| Update a Campaign (Change Pace)". |
| `confirm_campaign` | SAFETY SWITCH. Campaigns are created with confirm=false (a test: nothing is delivered). Set to true only when you really want the campaign to run. |
| `verified_by_user` | SAFETY SWITCH. Caller Number Certification. Set to true only if you can truthfully give the certification quoted on "POST \| Create a Caller Number". |
| `confirm_cancel` | SAFETY SWITCH. Canceling is final (the guide documents no way to undo it). Set to true to allow the Cancel requests to be sent. |
| `confirm_create_account` | SAFETY SWITCH. The guide documents no way to remove an account through the API. Set to true to allow "POST \| Create an Account" to be sent. |
| `postback_signing_secret` | Your account postback signing secret (set in the Postback settings). Used to verify the X-VoApps-Signature HMAC on inbound postbacks. Leave blank in a shared collection. |
| `sample_postback_destination` | Reference only (Postback Signature folder): the destination URL the sample signature is computed over. |
| `sample_postback_body` | Reference only (Postback Signature folder): the sample postback JSON the signature is computed over. |
| `sample_postback_timestamp` | Reference only (Postback Signature folder): unix-seconds timestamp set by the request pre-request script. |
| `computed_postback_signature` | Reference only (Postback Signature folder): the X-VoApps-Signature recomputed by the request scripts. |

Computed on every send (do not edit): `run_id`, `now_utc`, `now_utc_label`, `now_local_offset`, `today_utc`, `yesterday_utc`, `week_ago_utc`, `target_date`, `target_date_utc_label`, `target_date_local_offset`, `new_account_name`, `new_message_name`, `new_message_description`, `new_caller_number_name`, `new_campaign_name`.

## Saved examples

Each request carries saved examples. **Success examples come from the guide's own samples** (and every documented result code on "GET | Record Information"). **Error examples use the HTTP status codes the KB documents** (its *Errors & Status Codes* page): `400` validation with an `{"error":"..."}` body, plus `401` / `403` (`not_authorized`) / `404` (`not-found`) / `500`. Where the KB documents the exact message (e.g. "Name must be unique for this account") the example uses it; the few remaining paraphrases stay marked **"[Illustrative]"**. Use Postman's "Save as example" to replace them with real responses.

## Webhooks and results

When a record includes `voapps_postback_url`, VoApps sends an HTTP POST with the delivery result ([Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url)).

> **Retry behavior:** **Test it first:** point `voapps_postback_url` at a free [webhook.site](https://webhook.site) URL and send one record – you'll see exactly what VoApps posts back (the `X-VoApps-Timestamp` / `X-VoApps-Destination` / `X-VoApps-Signature` headers and the JSON body) before you build your real receiver.

| Result | Code | Triggers a postback? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | 100 | No |
| Running | 101 | No |
| Successfully delivered | 200 | Yes |
| Expired | 300 | Yes |
| Canceled | 301 | Yes |
| Unsuccessful delivery attempt | 400 | Yes |
| Not a wireless number | 401 | Yes |
| Duplicate number | 402 | Yes |
| Not a valid US number | 403 | Yes |
| Undeliverable | 404 | Yes |
| Not in service | 405 | Yes |
| Voicemail not setup | 406 | Yes |
| Voicemail full | 407 | Yes |
| Invalid caller number | 408 | Yes |
| Invalid message id | 409 | Yes |
| Prohibited self call | 410 | Yes |
| Restricted | 500 | Yes |
| Restricted for frequency | 501 | Yes |
| Restricted geographical region | 502 | Yes |
| Restricted individual number | 503 | Yes |
| Restricted WebRecon | 504 | Yes |

Timestamps (`voapps_timestamp`) are `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss UTC`, or `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss ±HH:MM` if your account uses account-timezone results file timestamps ([Results Timestamps](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/results-timestamps)). Result codes are explained in [Result Codes Defined](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#understanding/result-codes-defined).

## Learn more in the Knowledge Base

- [API Access Guide](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api) (the source for this collection)
- [API Integration Outline](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#integration) (planning an integration), including [The 10:00Z Start Rule](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#integration/the-10-00z-start-rule) and [UTC Date Logic](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#integration/utc-date-logic-implementation-pattern)
- [API FAQ](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/frequently-asked-questions) (webhooks, authentication, campaign values)
- [Understanding Your Results](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#understanding)
- [Pacing Calculator](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/creating-a-campaign-pace-setting)

Need access or help? Ask your VoApps account team.

item.name: Smoke Tests (run in order)
item.description:
**Run this folder top to bottom** (right-click the folder > Run folder, or click Send on each step in order). 31 numbered steps; each one saves what the next one needs.

| Part | Steps | What it does | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Read-only checks | 01-06 | Key works; lists and fetches accounts, messages, caller numbers, campaigns | An account with a message and a caller number |
| B. Test campaign and record | 07-11 | Creates one **unconfirmed** transactional campaign and one record, then reads them back | Part A (nothing is delivered while `confirm_campaign` is `false`) |
| C. Campaign controls | 12-17 | Cancel-without-pause (expects 4xx), pause, pace, unpause, pause, cancel | **Optional.** A running or paused campaign; `confirm_cancel` must be `true` for cancel steps |
| D. Partner API | 18-19 | Partner users and acting on a managed user's behalf | **Partners only** (`partner_api_key`) |
| E. Error handling | 20-31 | Bad key, no key, unknown ids, missing fields: each must be **rejected with a 4xx** | Part B for the campaign steps |

Tip: in the Collection Runner, untick parts C and D unless you need them. These steps reuse the requests in the folders below; the saved success examples (guide samples, every result code) live on those matching requests.

Safety defaults: campaigns are created with `confirm=false`, the caller-number certification is never made for you, and cancel/create-account are blocked until you flip their switch variables. See the collection description.

[API Access Guide](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api) · [VoApps Knowledge Base](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html)

item.description: Nothing is created. Confirms authentication and reads your account data.

request.description:
**Step 1 of 31. Start here.** Confirms your API key works and fills in `account_id`.

Lists the accounts for this API key. Hidden accounts are left out unless you add the `filter` query parameter (disabled here; see the "Hidden Only" and "All Including Hidden" variants).

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden accounts are excluded. Use `hidden` to return only hidden accounts, or `all` to return all accounts including hidden ones. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the account. |
| `name` | Name of the account. |
| `timezone` | Timezone of the account. |

**In this collection**

- Saves **account_id** for you (keeps your current one if it is still in the list).
- Tests: 2xx, JSON, `accounts` array, id/name/timezone on every account, IANA-style timezones, unique ids.

**VoApps Knowledge Base:** [API Access Guide – List Accounts](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/list-accounts) · [VoApps Knowledge Base](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html)

exec: pm.test('Response body is JSON', () => { body = pm.response.json(); });
const ok = body !== null && pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300;
const need = (obj, fields, label) => fields.forEach(f => pm.expect(obj, (label || 'object') + ' is missing "' + f + '"').to.have.property(f));
const isBlank = k => { const v = pm.variables.get(k); return v === undefined || v === null || String(v).trim() === ''; };
if (v === undefined || v === null || v === '') { return; }
if (useEnv) { pm.environment.set(k, v); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v); }
pm.test('Every account has id, name and timezone', () => body.accounts.forEach(a => need(a, ['id', 'name', 'timezone'], 'account')));
pm.test('Every timezone looks like an IANA timezone (Area/Location)', () => body.accounts.forEach(a => pm.expect(String(a.timezone)).to.match(/^[A-Za-z_]+\/[A-Za-z_\/]+$/)));
pm.test('Account ids are unique', () => { const ids = body.accounts.map(a => a.id); pm.expect(new Set(ids).size).to.eql(ids.length); });
pm.visualizer.set(template, { rows: rows.map(r => ({ id: r.id, name: r.name, timezone: r.timezone })) });

request.description:
Smoke test step. Read-only: nothing is created. Lists campaigns created in the last 7 days (may be empty).

Lists campaigns between `created_date_start` and `created_date_end` (YYYY-MM-DD UTC), newest first. Defaults to the last 7 days.

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account to query. |
| `created_date` | Required* | A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._ |
| `created_date_start` / `created_date_end` | Required* | Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._ |
| `page` | Optional | Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the campaign. |
| `name` | Name of the campaign. |
| `state` | Detailed state: created, targeted, throttled, confirmed, importing, delivering, running, completed, paused, paused_importing, canceled, or archived. **Use `status` for automation.** |
| `pace` | Current campaign pace (successful deliveries per hour). |
| `progress` | Campaign progress as a percentage (0–100). |
| `status` | Simplified status for automation: setup, importing, pending, running, completed, paused, canceled, or archived. |
| `uri` | URL to the campaign in the web interface. |
| `target_date` | Campaign target date/time in ISO 8601 format. |
| `export` | Current export file URL (updated as campaign progresses). |
| `records_count` | Total number of records in the campaign. |
| `successfully_delivered` | Number of records with a "Successfully delivered" result. |
| `caller_number` | Default caller number for the campaign. |
| `message_id` | Default message ID for the campaign. |

> **Info:** The `created_date` parameter refers to the date the campaign object was **first created in VoApps**. It is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (`target_date`), which is the date the campaign ran or is scheduled to run. If you do not know the `created_date`, use a broader created-date range and filter the returned campaigns by `target_date`.

**In this collection**

- Dates are UTC (YYYY-MM-DD). **today_utc** and **week_ago_utc** are computed for you on every send.
- Tests: 2xx, JSON, `campaigns` array, at most 25 per page, unique ids, and on every campaign: required fields, documented `status` values, numeric and 0 to 100 ranges, https `uri`/`export`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account to query. |
| `created_date` | Required* | A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._ |
| `created_date_start` / `created_date_end` | Required* | Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._ |
| `page` | Optional | Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the campaign. |
| `name` | Name of the campaign. |
| `state` | Detailed state: created, targeted, throttled, confirmed, importing, delivering, running, completed, paused, paused_importing, canceled, or archived. **Use `status` for automation.** |
| `pace` | Current campaign pace (successful deliveries per hour). |

| `target_date` | Campaign target date/time in ISO 8601 format. |
| `export` | Current export file URL (updated as campaign progresses). |
| `records_count` | Total number of records in the campaign. |
| `successfully_delivered` | Number of records with a "Successfully delivered" result. |
| `caller_number` | Default caller number for the campaign. |
| `message_id` | Default message ID for the campaign. |

> **Info:** The `created_date` parameter refers to the date the campaign object was **first created in VoApps**. It is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (`target_date`), which is the date the campaign ran or is scheduled to run. If you do not know the `created_date`, use a broader created-date range and filter the returned campaigns by `target_date`.

request.description:
Adds one record (the guide's sample number) to the step 7 campaign. Nothing is delivered while the campaign is unconfirmed.

Adds one phone number to a **transactional** campaign. The preferred route: it names the campaign explicitly (`campaign_id`).

`POST {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns/{{campaign_id}}/records`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account where this campaign resides. |
| `campaign_id` | In URI | The ID of the transactional campaign to add the record to. |
| `record_attributes` | Required | JSON representation of the record. See supported fields below. |

**record_attributes JSON fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Field | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` or `phone_number` | Required | The phone number to deliver the message to. |
| `voapps_caller_number` | Optional | Override the campaign's default caller number for this record. Use the actual **phone number** (e.g. +15555551212), not the id of a saved [caller number](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/caller-numbers). |
| `voapps_message_id` | Optional | Override the campaign's default message for this record. |
| `voapps_zip_code` | Optional | Zip code to assist with timezone detection for delivery window enforcement. |
| `voapps_voice_append` | Optional | Voice append identifier. |
| `voapps_postback_url` | Optional | We'll POST this record's result to the URL once the record completes. Must use **https** with a valid certificate and a publicly reachable host; plain http, private or internal addresses, and redirecting endpoints are skipped without retries. With an org **signing secret** ([Settings](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/team-organization-settings)), each postback carries an X-VoApps-Signature header – see [Verifying Postbacks](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/verifying-postbacks). Full payload and result codes: [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url). |
| `voapps_target_date` | Optional | Target delivery time for this individual record (UTC, ISO 8601). Runs immediately if not specified. |
| _additional fields_ | Optional | Any additional JSON fields are included in the export CSV but not returned in API calls. |

> **Info:** Field names (CSV headers and JSON keys) are **case-insensitive**, but spelling and underscores must match the documented names; values keep the case you submit. Phone numbers accept 10-digit or `+1` format. In webhook payloads and the [Record Information](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/record-information) GET response, `record.number` is normalized to `+1` format, while `original_fields` preserves exactly what you submitted.

> **A duplicate isn't an API error.** `402` is a delivery result code, separate from the HTTP status – your `POST` still returns normally. See [Errors & Status Codes](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/errors-and-status-codes) and [Result Codes Defined](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#understanding/result-codes-defined).

> **Don't generate `duplicate_hash` yourself.** VoApps creates it automatically; it isn't a fingerprint of your data and doesn't work as a client idempotency key. Re-submitting the same number just creates more retained duplicate records.

**In this collection**

- `record_attributes` is a JSON string in a form-encoded body, as in the guide's `-d record_attributes='{...}'` example.
- The sample postback URL (`your-url.example.com`) does not exist; replace **voapps_postback_url** with your own HTTPS endpoint to receive results.
- Saves **record_id**.

item.name: Campaigns
item.description:
Create, monitor and control campaigns. [Guide: Campaigns](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/campaigns)

The update requests depend on the campaign's current state (unpause and cancel need a paused campaign), so send them one at a time. **Smoke Tests, part C** runs them in a working order: pause, change pace, unpause, pause, cancel.

query.description: Required* – A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._
Required* – Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._
Required* – Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._
Optional – Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items.
Optional – Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`.

request.description:
Lists campaigns for one date (`created_date`, YYYY-MM-DD UTC). Use `created_date` **or** the start/end pair, not both.

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account to query. |
| `created_date` | Required* | A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._ |
| `created_date_start` / `created_date_end` | Required* | Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._ |
| `page` | Optional | Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the campaign. |
| `name` | Name of the campaign. |
| `state` | Detailed state: created, targeted, throttled, confirmed, importing, delivering, running, completed, paused, paused_importing, canceled, or archived. **Use `status` for automation.** |
| `pace` | Current campaign pace (successful deliveries per hour). |
| `progress` | Campaign progress as a percentage (0–100). |
| `status` | Simplified status for automation: setup, importing, pending, running, completed, paused, canceled, or archived. |
| `uri` | URL to the campaign in the web interface. |
| `target_date` | Campaign target date/time in ISO 8601 format. |
| `export` | Current export file URL (updated as campaign progresses). |
| `records_count` | Total number of records in the campaign. |
| `successfully_delivered` | Number of records with a "Successfully delivered" result. |
| `caller_number` | Default caller number for the campaign. |
| `message_id` | Default message ID for the campaign. |

> **Info:** The `created_date` parameter refers to the date the campaign object was **first created in VoApps**. It is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (`target_date`), which is the date the campaign ran or is scheduled to run. If you do not know the `created_date`, use a broader created-date range and filter the returned campaigns by `target_date`.

const ok = body !== null && pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300;
const need = (obj, fields, label) => fields.forEach(f => pm.expect(obj, (label || 'object') + ' is missing "' + f + '"').to.have.property(f));
const isBlank = k => { const v = pm.variables.get(k); return v === undefined || v === null || String(v).trim() === ''; };
if (v === undefined || v === null || v === '') { return; }
if (useEnv) { pm.environment.set(k, v); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v); }
pm.test('A page holds at most 25 campaigns', () => pm.expect(body.campaigns.length).to.be.at.most(25));
pm.test('Campaign ids are unique', () => { const ids = body.campaigns.map(c => c.id); pm.expect(new Set(ids).size).to.eql(ids.length); });
pm.test('Each campaign has id, name, state, status and uri', () => items.forEach(c => need(c, ['id', 'name', 'state', 'status', 'uri'], 'campaign')));
pm.test('status is one of the documented values (' + STATUS.join(', ') + ')', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(STATUS, 'status "' + c.status + '"').to.include(c.status)));
pm.test('state is a non-empty string', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.state).length).to.be.above(0)));
items.forEach(c => { if (STATE.indexOf(c.state) < 0) { soft('state "' + c.state + '" is not in the documented state list'); } });
pm.test('uri is an https VoApps campaign link', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.uri)).to.match(/^https:\/\/[^\s]+\/accounts\/\d+\/campaigns\/\d+/)));

pm.test('progress is between 0 and 100 when present', () => items.forEach(c => { if (c.progress !== undefined && c.progress !== null && c.progress !== '') { pm.expect(Number(c.progress)).to.be.within(0, 100); } }));

pm.test('pace, records_count and successfully_delivered are numeric when present', () => items.forEach(c => ['pace', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered'].forEach(f => { if (c[f] !== undefined && c[f] !== null && c[f] !== '') { pm.expect(Number.isFinite(Number(c[f])), f + ' = ' + c[f]).to.eql(true); } })));

pm.test('successfully_delivered does not exceed records_count', () => items.forEach(c => { if (Number.isFinite(Number(c.records_count)) && Number.isFinite(Number(c.successfully_delivered))) { pm.expect(Number(c.successfully_delivered)).to.be.at.most(Number(c.records_count)); } }));

items.forEach(c => { if (c.caller_number && !/^\+\d{10,15}$/.test(String(c.caller_number))) { soft('caller_number "' + c.caller_number + '" is not in +E.164 format'); } });

items.forEach(c => { const missing = ['pace', 'progress', 'target_date', 'export', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered', 'caller_number', 'message_id'].filter(f => !(f in c)); if (missing.length) { soft('campaign ' + c.id + ' is missing documented field(s): ' + missing.join(', ')); } });

request.description:
Lists campaigns between `created_date_start` and `created_date_end` (YYYY-MM-DD UTC), newest first. Defaults to the last 7 days.

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account to query. |
| `created_date` | Required* | A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._ |
| `created_date_start` / `created_date_end` | Required* | Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._ |
| `page` | Optional | Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the campaign. |
| `name` | Name of the campaign. |
| `state` | Detailed state: created, targeted, throttled, confirmed, importing, delivering, running, completed, paused, paused_importing, canceled, or archived. **Use `status` for automation.** |
| `pace` | Current campaign pace (successful deliveries per hour). |
| `progress` | Campaign progress as a percentage (0–100). |
| `status` | Simplified status for automation: setup, importing, pending, running, completed, paused, canceled, or archived. |
| `uri` | URL to the campaign in the web interface. |
| `target_date` | Campaign target date/time in ISO 8601 format. |
| `export` | Current export file URL (updated as campaign progresses). |
| `records_count` | Total number of records in the campaign. |
| `successfully_delivered` | Number of records with a "Successfully delivered" result. |
| `caller_number` | Default caller number for the campaign. |
| `message_id` | Default message ID for the campaign. |

> **Info:** The `created_date` parameter refers to the date the campaign object was **first created in VoApps**. It is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (`target_date`), which is the date the campaign ran or is scheduled to run. If you do not know the `created_date`, use a broader created-date range and filter the returned campaigns by `target_date`.

**In this collection**

- Dates are UTC (YYYY-MM-DD). **today_utc** and **week_ago_utc** are computed for you on every send.

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account to query. |
| `created_date` | Required* | A single date (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) to scope campaigns. This is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (its `target_date`) – the date the campaign ran or will run – rather it's the date the campaign object was **first created in the system**. Add time and offset to adjust timezone, e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`. _*Required if date range not provided._ |
| `created_date_start` / `created_date_end` | Required* | Date range (YYYY-MM-DD UTC) bounding the date the campaign was first transmitted to VoApps. Results sorted newest first. _*Required if created_date not provided._ |
| `page` | Optional | Page number for pagination (default: 1). Each page contains 25 items. |
| `filter` | Optional | Without a filter, hidden campaigns are excluded. Use `hidden` or `all`. |

**Response fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Internal ID of the campaign. |
| `name` | Name of the campaign. |
| `state` | Detailed state: created, targeted, throttled, confirmed, importing, delivering, running, completed, paused, paused_importing, canceled, or archived. **Use `status` for automation.** |
| `pace` | Current campaign pace (successful deliveries per hour). |
| `progress` | Campaign progress as a percentage (0–100). |
| `status` | Simplified status for automation: setup, importing, pending, running, completed, paused, canceled, or archived. |
| `uri` | URL to the campaign in the web interface. |
| `target_date` | Campaign target date/time in ISO 8601 format. |
| `export` | Current export file URL (updated as campaign progresses). |
| `records_count` | Total number of records in the campaign. |
| `successfully_delivered` | Number of records with a "Successfully delivered" result. |
| `caller_number` | Default caller number for the campaign. |
| `message_id` | Default message ID for the campaign. |

> **Info:** The `created_date` parameter refers to the date the campaign object was **first created in VoApps**. It is **not** the campaign's scheduled run date (`target_date`), which is the date the campaign ran or is scheduled to run. exec: pm.test('Response body is JSON', () => { body = pm.response.json(); });
const ok = body !== null && pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300;
const need = (obj, fields, label) => fields.forEach(f => pm.expect(obj, (label || 'object') + ' is missing "' + f + '"').to.have.property(f));
pm.test('A page holds at most 25 campaigns', () => pm.expect(body.campaigns.length).to.be.at.most(25));
pm.test('Campaign ids are unique', () => { const ids = body.campaigns.map(c => c.id); pm.expect(new Set(ids).size).to.eql(ids.length); });
pm.test('Each campaign has id, name, state, status and uri', () => items.forEach(c => need(c, ['id', 'name', 'state', 'status', 'uri'], 'campaign')));
pm.test('status is one of the documented values (' + STATUS.join(', ') + ')', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(STATUS, 'status "' + c.status + '"').to.include(c.status)));
pm.test('state is a non-empty string', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.state).length).to.be.above(0)));
items.forEach(c => { if (STATE.indexOf(c.state) < 0) { soft('state "' + c.state + '" is not in the documented state list'); } });
pm.test('uri is an https VoApps campaign link', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.uri)).to.match(/^https:\/\/[^\s]+\/accounts\/\d+\/campaigns\/\d+/)));

pm.test('progress is between 0 and 100 when present', () => items.forEach(c => { if (c.progress !== undefined && c.progress !== null && c.progress !== '') { pm.expect(Number(c.progress)).to.be.within(0, 100); } }));

pm.test('pace, records_count and successfully_delivered are numeric when present', () => items.forEach(c => ['pace', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered'].forEach(f => { if (c[f] !== undefined && c[f] !== null && c[f] !== '') { pm.expect(Number.isFinite(Number(c[f])), f + ' = ' + c[f]).to.eql(true); } })));

pm.test('successfully_delivered does not exceed records_count', () => items.forEach(c => { if (Number.isFinite(Number(c.records_count)) && Number.isFinite(Number(c.successfully_delivered))) { pm.expect(Number(c.successfully_delivered)).to.be.at.most(Number(c.records_count)); } }));
pm.test('export is an https file link when present', () => items.forEach(c => { if (c.export) { pm.expect(String(c.export)).to.match(/^https:\/\//); } }));
items.forEach(c => { if (c.caller_number && !/^\+\d{10,15}$/.test(String(c.caller_number))) { soft('caller_number "' + c.caller_number + '" is not in +E.164 format'); } });

items.forEach(c => { const missing = ['pace', 'progress', 'target_date', 'export', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered', 'caller_number', 'message_id'].filter(f => !(f in c)); if (missing.length) { soft('campaign ' + c.id + ' is missing documented field(s): ' + missing.join(', ')); } });

formdata.description: Required – ID of the message for this campaign. Must be owned by the specified account.

Required – The number to display as caller ID during delivery. Use the actual **phone number** (e.g. +15555551212), not the id of a saved [caller number](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/caller-numbers).
Required* – CSV file of phone numbers. Required for non-transactional campaigns; optional for transactional.
Required (unique) – Campaign name. **Must be unique per account** to prevent duplicate submissions via repeated API calls.

Optional – When to start the campaign. Use ISO 8601 format anchored to UTC – a "Z" suffix (e.g. `2026-10-06T15:16:39.074Z`), an explicit UTC offset (e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`), or a plain "UTC" label (e.g. `2026-10-06 15:16:39 UTC`) are all accepted. Runs immediately if not specified.
Optional – Set to `true` for a transactional campaign. Records can be added until the campaign completes. Default: `false`.
Optional – Must be `true` for the campaign to run. Leave blank or `false` to test campaign creation without delivery.

Optional – Successful deliveries per hour. Numeric value 50–8000. Values outside this range are rounded to the nearest allowed value. Leave blank to deliver as fast as possible. See the [Pacing Calculator](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/creating-a-campaign-pace-setting) for a recommended starting value.

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |

exec: pm.test('Response body is JSON', () => { body = pm.response.json(); });
const ok = body !== null && pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300;
const need = (obj, fields, label) => fields.forEach(f => pm.expect(obj, (label || 'object') + ' is missing "' + f + '"').to.have.property(f));
const isBlank = k => { const v = pm.variables.get(k); return v === undefined || v === null || String(v).trim() === ''; };
if (v === undefined || v === null || v === '') { return; }
if (useEnv) { pm.environment.set(k, v); } else { pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v); }
pm.test('"campaign" is an object with id, name, uri and target_date', () => { pm.expect(body.campaign).to.be.an('object'); need(body.campaign, ['id', 'name', 'uri', 'target_date'], 'campaign'); });
pm.test('Name echoes the unique name that was sent', () => pm.expect(body.campaign.name).to.eql(pm.variables.get('new_campaign_name')));
pm.test('uri is an https link into this account\'s campaigns', () => pm.expect(String(body.campaign.uri)).to.include('/accounts/' + pm.variables.get('account_id') + '/campaigns/'));

request.description:
`target_date` is left out (disabled), so the campaign runs immediately once confirmed ("Runs immediately if not specified").

`POST {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account where this campaign should be created. |
| `message_id` | Required | ID of the message for this campaign. Must be owned by the specified account. |
| `caller_number` | Required | The number to display as caller ID during delivery. Use the actual **phone number** (e.g. +15555551212), not the id of a saved [caller number](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/caller-numbers). |
| `campaign_import` | Required* | CSV file of phone numbers. Required for non-transactional campaigns; optional for transactional. |
| `name` | Required (unique) | Campaign name. **Must be unique per account** to prevent duplicate submissions via repeated API calls. |
| `target_date` | Optional | When to start the campaign. Use ISO 8601 format anchored to UTC – a "Z" suffix (e.g. `2026-10-06T15:16:39.074Z`), an explicit UTC offset (e.g. `2026-10-06 11:16:39 -04:00`), or a plain "UTC" label (e.g. `2026-10-06 15:16:39 UTC`) are all accepted. Runs immediately if not specified. |
| `transactional` | Optional | Set to `true` for a transactional campaign. Records can be added until the campaign completes. Default: `false`. |
| `confirm` | Optional | Must be `true` for the campaign to run. Leave blank or `false` to test campaign creation without delivery. |
| `pace` | Optional | Successful deliveries per hour. Numeric value 50–8000. Values outside this range are rounded to the nearest allowed value. Leave blank to deliver as fast as possible. See the [Pacing Calculator](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/creating-a-campaign-pace-setting) for a recommended starting value. |

> **Note:** Reusing a `name` within the same account returns `400 Bad Request` with `Name must be unique for this account` – it does not create a second campaign. Use a unique name (append an ISO 8601 date-time), create the campaign once and then add records, and check your response codes. See [Error Handling & Campaign Names](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#integration/error-handling-and-campaign-names) in the API Integration Outline.

**In this collection**

- Safe by default: **confirm** is `{{confirm_campaign}}` (`false`), which the guide describes as "test campaign creation without delivery".
- Name is `postman-test-campaign-<timestamp>`, because campaign names must be unique per account.
- Saves **campaign_id**.
- Tests: 2xx, JSON, `campaign` has id/name/uri/target_date, name echoes what was sent, uri points into this account's campaigns.

request.description:
Fetches one campaign's status and details.

`GET {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns/{{campaign_id}}`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account. |
| `campaign_id` | In URI | The ID of the campaign to retrieve. |

> **Info:** The `export` URL points to a file hosted on AWS S3, and the link **expires after 7 days**. If it has expired, generate a fresh one with another request to this endpoint, or by clicking **Export CSV** in the VoApps client web portal.

**In this collection**

- Tests: 2xx, JSON, campaign fields, documented `status` values, numeric/range checks, returned id matches **campaign_id**, uri points into this account.

**VoApps Knowledge Base:** [API Access Guide – Campaign Information](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/campaign-information) · [Campaign status and state values (FAQ)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/what-are-the-possible-values-for-status) · [VoApps Knowledge Base](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html)

exec: pm.test('Response body is JSON', () => { body = pm.response.json(); });
const ok = body !== null && pm.response.code >= 200 && pm.response.code < 300;
const need = (obj, fields, label) => fields.forEach(f => pm.expect(obj, (label || 'object') + ' is missing "' + f + '"').to.have.property(f));
pm.test('Each campaign has id, name, state, status and uri', () => items.forEach(c => need(c, ['id', 'name', 'state', 'status', 'uri'], 'campaign')));
pm.test('status is one of the documented values (' + STATUS.join(', ') + ')', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(STATUS, 'status "' + c.status + '"').to.include(c.status)));
pm.test('state is a non-empty string', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.state).length).to.be.above(0)));
items.forEach(c => { if (STATE.indexOf(c.state) < 0) { soft('state "' + c.state + '" is not in the documented state list'); } });
pm.test('uri is an https VoApps campaign link', () => items.forEach(c => pm.expect(String(c.uri)).to.match(/^https:\/\/[^\s]+\/accounts\/\d+\/campaigns\/\d+/)));

pm.test('progress is between 0 and 100 when present', () => items.forEach(c => { if (c.progress !== undefined && c.progress !== null && c.progress !== '') { pm.expect(Number(c.progress)).to.be.within(0, 100); } }));

pm.test('pace, records_count and successfully_delivered are numeric when present', () => items.forEach(c => ['pace', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered'].forEach(f => { if (c[f] !== undefined && c[f] !== null && c[f] !== '') { pm.expect(Number.isFinite(Number(c[f])), f + ' = ' + c[f]).to.eql(true); } })));

pm.test('successfully_delivered does not exceed records_count', () => items.forEach(c => { if (Number.isFinite(Number(c.records_count)) && Number.isFinite(Number(c.successfully_delivered))) { pm.expect(Number(c.successfully_delivered)).to.be.at.most(Number(c.records_count)); } }));
pm.test('export is an https file link when present', () => items.forEach(c => { if (c.export) { pm.expect(String(c.export)).to.match(/^https:\/\//); } }));
items.forEach(c => { if (c.caller_number && !/^\+\d{10,15}$/.test(String(c.caller_number))) { soft('caller_number "' + c.caller_number + '" is not in +E.164 format'); } });

items.forEach(c => { const missing = ['pace', 'progress', 'target_date', 'export', 'records_count', 'successfully_delivered', 'caller_number', 'message_id'].filter(f => !(f in c)); if (missing.length) { soft('campaign ' + c.id + ' is missing documented field(s): ' + missing.join(', ')); } });
pm.test('uri points into this account', () => pm.expect(String(body.campaign.uri)).to.include('/accounts/' + pm.variables.get('account_id') + '/'));

request.description:
Pauses a campaign (`method=pause`). A campaign must be paused before it can be canceled.

`PUT {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns/{{campaign_id}}`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account where this campaign resides. |
| `campaign_id` | In URI | The ID of the campaign to update. |
| `method` | Optional | Action to perform: `pause`, `unpause`, or `cancel`. A campaign must be paused before it can be canceled. |
| `pace` | Optional | New pacing value (deliveries per hour). Same range as campaign creation (50–8000). See the [Pacing Calculator](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/creating-a-campaign-pace-setting) for help picking a number. |

**In this collection**

item.name: Transactional Records
item.description: Add numbers one at a time and read their results. [Guide: Transactional Records](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/transactional-records) · [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url)

urlencoded.description: Required – JSON representation of the record. See supported fields below.

request.description:
Adds one phone number to a **transactional** campaign. The preferred route: it names the campaign explicitly (`campaign_id`).

`POST {{base_url}}/accounts/{{account_id}}/campaigns/{{campaign_id}}/records`

**Parameters** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Parameter | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization Token` | In header | Include the token to authenticate. |
| `account_id` | In URI | The ID of the account where this campaign resides. |
| `campaign_id` | In URI | The ID of the transactional campaign to add the record to. |
| `record_attributes` | Required | JSON representation of the record. See supported fields below. |

**record_attributes JSON fields** (quoted from the API Access Guide)

| Field | Note | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` or `phone_number` | Required | The phone number to deliver the message to. |
| `voapps_caller_number` | Optional | Override the campaign's default caller number for this record. Use the actual **phone number** (e.g. +15555551212), not the id of a saved [caller number](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/caller-numbers). |
| `voapps_message_id` | Optional | Override the campaign's default message for this record. |
| `voapps_zip_code` | Optional | Zip code to assist with timezone detection for delivery window enforcement. |
| `voapps_voice_append` | Optional | Voice append identifier. |
| `voapps_postback_url` | Optional | We'll POST this record's result to the URL once the record completes. Must use **https** with a valid certificate and a publicly reachable host; plain http, private or internal addresses, and redirecting endpoints are skipped without retries. With an org **signing secret** ([Settings](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#user/team-organization-settings)), each postback carries an X-VoApps-Signature header – see [Verifying Postbacks](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/verifying-postbacks). Full payload and result codes: [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url). |
| `voapps_target_date` | Optional | Target delivery time for this individual record (UTC, ISO 8601). Runs immediately if not specified. |
| _additional fields_ | Optional | Any additional JSON fields are included in the export CSV but not returned in API calls. |

> **Info:** Field names (CSV headers and JSON keys) are **case-insensitive**, but spelling and underscores must match the documented names; values keep the case you submit. Phone numbers accept 10-digit or `+1` format. In webhook payloads and the [Record Information](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/record-information) GET response, `record.number` is normalized to `+1` format, while `original_fields` preserves exactly what you submitted.

> **A duplicate isn't an API error.** `402` is a delivery result code, separate from the HTTP status – your `POST` still returns normally. See [Errors & Status Codes](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/errors-and-status-codes) and [Result Codes Defined](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#understanding/result-codes-defined).

> **Don't generate `duplicate_hash` yourself.** VoApps creates it automatically; it isn't a fingerprint of your data and doesn't work as a client idempotency key. Re-submitting the same number just creates more retained duplicate records.

**In this collection**

- `record_attributes` is a JSON string in a form-encoded body, as in the guide's `-d record_attributes='{...}'` example.
- The sample postback URL (`your-url.example.com`) does not exist; replace **voapps_postback_url** with your own HTTPS endpoint to receive results.
- Saves **record_id**.
- Tests: 2xx, JSON, `record.id` present and positive.

**VoApps Knowledge Base:** [API Access Guide – Create a Record](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/create-a-record) · [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url) · [The 10:00Z Start Rule](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#integration/the-10-00z-start-rule) · [Results Timestamps](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/results-timestamps) · [VoApps Knowledge Base](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html)

item.name: Postback Signature (verify)
item.description: Verify the HMAC signature on inbound DirectDrop Voicemail postbacks before trusting them. [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url)

request.description: Reference only — you do **not** send this to VoApps. VoApps POSTs each delivery result to your `voapps_postback_url` with `X-VoApps-Timestamp`, `X-VoApps-Destination` and `X-VoApps-Signature` (`v1=` + HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp.destination.raw_body`, keyed with your account **postback signing secret**). The **pre-request script** shows how VoApps signs; the **test script** shows how your endpoint verifies: recompute from the received headers and raw body, then compare. Set `postback_signing_secret` to run it with your own secret. [Webhook (Postback URL)](https://voapps.com/hubfs/Client_Success/VoApps_Knowledge_Base.html#api/webhook-postback-url)

exec: // HOW VOAPPS SIGNS A POSTBACK (this reference request simulates it)
// signing string = timestamp + "." + destination + "." + rawBody   (joined by literal dots)
// header value   = "v1=" + HMAC-SHA256(signingString, <your postback signing secret>)  in hex
const sig  = 'v1=' + CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(ts + '.' + dest + '.' + body, secret).toString(CryptoJS.enc.Hex);
// HOW YOUR ENDPOINT VERIFIES A RECEIVED POSTBACK
// Recompute from the received X-VoApps-Timestamp / -Destination headers and the RAW body,
// then compare to the X-VoApps-Signature header. In production use a constant-time compare,
// and optionally reject timestamps older than a few minutes (replay protection).
const received = pm.collectionVariables.get('computed_postback_signature'); // production: the 'X-VoApps-Signature' request header
const expected = 'v1=' + CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(ts + '.' + dest + '.' + rawBody, secret).toString(CryptoJS.enc.Hex);
pm.test('Recomputed HMAC-SHA256 matches the X-VoApps-Signature header', () => pm.expect(expected).to.eql(received));
